newsitem.title: BELGIUM: Belgian region, Duferco agree draft Clabecq deal.
newsitem.headline: Belgian region, Duferco agree draft Clabecq deal.

text.p: Officials from the Belgian Walloon region, its SWS steel investment arm and Italian-Swiss firm Duferco have reached a draft agreement for a partial takeover of bankrupt Belgian steel firm Clabecq, the Walloon government said in a statement on Wednesday.

The three parties had reached an agreement on a letter of intent for the takeover of some of Forges de Clabecq's activities with a view to recreating an integrated steelworks, the brief statement said. It gave no details.
"This agreement will be put to the Walloon Government and the SWS board for approval as soon as possible," it added.

It said the plan had been presented to Clabecq's court-appointed receivers. They would be sent a formal proposition by the SWS and Duferco in the coming days. Duferco, a private steel and commodities trader, announced in April it was studying a possible takeover of Clabecq.
Receivers have been trying to find a buyer for Clabecq and save the jobs of the firm's 1,800 workers ever since the company was declared bankrupt in January.
Clabecq is majority-owned by the Walloon Region.
Duferco has offered to invest up to three billion francs in Clabecq over five years and hand over one billion francs for the costs of early retirement and redundancy payments.

However it has insisted that a takeover was conditional on an end to unrest among Clabecq's dissatisfied workers who have clashed with police during several demonstrations over the threat to their jobs.
